content: Famotidine is an oral medication that inhibits gastric acid secretion. It is FDA-approved for the treatment of conditions such as heartburn, gastric hypersecretion, gastric ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and indigestion. Common side effects include constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, and headache. Adult Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications: Famotidine is indicated for the treatment of duodenal ulcers, esophagitis associated with GERD, gastric hypersecretion, gastric ulcers, GERD, and indigestion. Dosage Instructions: To relieve symptoms, take one tablet with a glass of water. Do not chew the tablet. To prevent symptoms, take one tablet with a glass of water 10 to 60 minutes before consuming food or beverages that may cause heartburn. Do not exceed two tablets in a 24-hour period. Off-Label Uses: Famotidine may be used for conditions such as maintenance therapy for esophagitis, gastritis, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, stress ulcers, and urticaria. However, these uses are not guideline-supported. Off-Label Dosage: For acute duodenal ulcer disease: 40 mg orally once daily at bedtime or 20 mg orally twice daily. For maintenance of duodenal ulcer disease: 20 mg orally once daily at bedtime. For short-term treatment of esophagitis associated with GERD: 20 to 40 mg orally twice daily for up to 12 weeks. For gastric hypersecretion: 20 to 160 mg orally every 6 hours. For short-term treatment of gastric ulcers: 40 mg orally once daily at bedtime. For short-term symptom relief of GERD: 20 mg orally twice daily for up to 6 weeks. For indigestion: 10 to 20 mg orally twice daily. Pediatric Indications and Dosage FDA-Labeled Indications: Famotidine is approved for use in children aged 12 years and older for the treatment of duodenal ulcers, esophagitis associated with GERD, gastric hypersecretion, gastric ulcers, GERD, and indigestion. Dosage for Children 12 Years and Older: To relieve symptoms, take one tablet with a glass of water. Do not chew the tablet. To prevent symptoms, take one tablet with a glass of water 10 to 60 minutes before consuming food or beverages that may cause heartburn. Do not exceed two tablets in a 24-hour period. Dosage for Children Under 12 Years: Consult a doctor before use. Off-Label Pediatric Use: Famotidine may be used for stress ulcer prophylaxis in children over 1 year of age. Off-Label Pediatric Dosage: For duodenal ulcer disease in children over 1 year: 0.5 mg/kg/day orally at bedtime or divided into two doses daily, with a maximum dose of 40 mg/day. For short-term treatment of gastric ulcers in children over 1 year: 0.5 mg/kg/day orally at bedtime or divided into two doses daily, with a maximum dose of 40 mg/day. Contraindications and Warnings Do not use famotidine if you are allergic to it or other acid reducers. Do not use this medication if you experience difficulty or pain swallowing food, vomiting blood, or have bloody or black stools, as these may indicate a serious condition. Consult a doctor if you have kidney disease before using this medication. Do not use famotidine in combination with other acid reducers. Consult a Doctor Before Use If: You have experienced heartburn for more than three months, as this may indicate a more serious condition. You have heartburn accompanied by lightheadedness, sweating, or dizziness. You experience chest pain or shoulder pain with shortness of breath, sweating, pain radiating to the arms, neck, or shoulders, or lightheadedness. You have frequent chest pain, wheezing, unexplained weight loss, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain. Stop Use and Consult a Doctor If: Your heartburn persists or worsens. You need to use this product for more than 14 days. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Consult a healthcare professional before use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Adverse Reactions Common Side Effects: Gastrointestinal: Constipation, diarrhea. Neurologic: Dizziness, headache. Serious Side Effects: Dermatologic: Rare cases of Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Gastrointestinal: Necrotizing enterocolitis in fetuses or newborns. Immunologic: Rare cases of anaphylaxis and angioedema. Musculoskeletal: Rhabdomyolysis. Neurologic: Rare cases of seizures. Respiratory: Rare cases of interstitial pneumonia and nosocomial pneumonia. Drug Interactions There is limited information available regarding drug interactions with famotidine. Use in Specific Populations There is no specific FDA guidance on the use of famotidine in pregnant women, nursing mothers, pediatric patients, geriatric patients, or individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no guidance on its use in specific gender or racial populations, or in immunocompromised patients. Administration and Monitoring Famotidine is administered orally. There is limited information available regarding monitoring requirements for this medication. Storage Store famotidine at a temperature of 20°-25°C (68°-77°F). Protect the medication from moisture and light. Alcohol Interaction The interaction between alcohol and famotidine has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of alcohol consumption while taking this medication. Brand Names Famotidine is marketed under the brand name 7 SELECT ACID CONTROLLER.
